title: Streaming connection quarantine and idempotency guidance to mitigate 5xx/timeouts during tenant surges
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
During a high-severity customer escalation (multiple enterprise tenants), we observed correlated 5xx errors, elevated tail latencies, and timeouts originating from long-lived streaming / chunked responses. The immediate impact: customer websocket/stream clients experienced mid-stream failures and SDK-level retries amplified load behind gateways and created connection-pool pressure across Hosted fleet and Dedicated peered pools. This ticket owns the engineering fix and operational guidance: implement a tenant-scoped streaming quarantine, conservative streaming keepalive/drop rules, idempotency guidance for SDK retries, and a short-term mitigation rollout to reduce customer-visible errors while we validate the runtime patch.
steps_taken:
1) Detection: On 2026-03-09 18:04 UTC Pager duty alerted for spike in 502/504 from streaming endpoints (chat.stream and generate/stream).
2) Triage: Tracing pointed to proxy->runtime half-open connections where KV cache eviction coincided with socket write stalls.
3) Temporary mitigation (hotfix): Rolled out conservative stream idle TTL change from 90s->20s on proxy to abort orphaned streams and returned immediate 5xx for inflight requests rather than leaving sockets hanging. Deployed tenant-scoped connection shedding for top 20 most active tenants to reduce head-of-line effects.
4) Customer comms: Incident Slack channel opened, support notified impacted tenants, and a targeted status update was posted to status.redwood.ai.
5) Post-mitigation monitoring: Error rate dropped by ~62% for affected tenants, overall P99 latency improved but some clients observed increased early failures—tradeoff accepted for system stability.
decisions:
- Implement tenant-scoped streaming quarantine layer in front of runtime that places aggressive backpressure on tenants that exceed configured streaming concurrency.
- Enforce idempotency tokens in client SDKs for non-streaming requests and provide guidance for stream reconnection semantics.
- Do not increase global connection pool size as a long-term solution; root cause is request amplification plus streaming stalls.
- Rollout runtime patch first to Hosted, then Dedicated, and finally enable as an opt-in for Private deployments via feature flag.
- Require automated chaos test that simulates KV eviction during active streams as part of CI for runtime-2.12.
postmortem_summary:
Root cause: interaction between long-lived streaming responses, KV cache compaction, and our connection multiplexing layer. When cache compaction triggered large KV writes, the runtime scheduler deprioritized active stream write flushes resulting in backpressure at the proxy. The proxy kept connections open while SDKs retried, producing a feedback loop that exhausted per-host file descriptors and produced 502/504 responses for other tenants.
Contributing factors: lack of per-tenant streaming concurrency limits, conservative stream abort TTL, and SDKs that retried streams without idempotency or guidance.
Outcome: Immediate mitigations reduced customer impact; runtime and proxy changes planned to prevent recurrence.
next_steps:
- Deploy runtime patch (PR 1228) to canary pool (hosts in us-west-2) by 2026-03-15.
- Merge proxy change (PR 654) to add tenant-quarantine and stream abort metrics, then rollout to primary edge by 2026-03-16.
- Publish SDK guidance doc and release SDK versions with idempotency helpers by 2026-03-18.
- Add tenant-level telemetry and alerts: streaming-concurrency saturating, stream_abort_rate, idempotency-missing-rate.
- Run chaos test simulating KV compaction under load on 2026-03-19 and include results in release notes.
- Schedule post-release review with Support and Solutions on 2026-03-22.
notes: We intentionally chose conservative early-abort behavior for streams because letting sockets linger made the system less available for other tenants.
Dedicated customers with private networks will get opt-in tooling because some have longer-lived streaming expectations—coordinate with Success before enabling.
This change may increase short-lived client errors; product and support should prepare templated messages and SDKs should implement reconnect-with-resume patterns where possible.
